author: AI Editorial Team (Esi)
key_learning_objective: Distinguish clinical manifestations of left-sided heart failure.
question_stem: A nurse is assessing a client with left-sided heart failure. Which findings does the nurse expect? Select all that apply.

rationales.A: Correct. Left-sided failure backs blood into the lungs, producing pulmonary congestion and crackles.
rationales.B: Correct. Pulmonary congestion causes dyspnea and orthopnea (LEFT = Lungs).
rationales.C: JVD is a systemic congestion sign of right-sided failure.
rationales.D: Correct. Frothy, pink/blood-tinged sputum reflects pulmonary edema from left-sided failure.
rationales.E: Peripheral edema is a right-sided (systemic) finding.
rationales.F: Ascites results from systemic venous congestion in right-sided failure.

key_takeaway: LEFT = Lungs (crackles, dyspnea, frothy sputum). RIGHT = Rest of body (edema, JVD, ascites).
nclex_test_taking_tip: Sort each finding by mechanism: lung congestion = left, systemic congestion = right.
memory_trick: LEFT = Lungs, RIGHT = Rest of body.
clinical_pearls: Frothy pink sputum signals acute pulmonary edema - a red flag.
Orthopnea: ask how many pillows they sleep on.
references: Left vs right heart failure pathophysiology
